awarding_body.detail: Aurora Education Foundation is confirmed as the establishing/administrating body on its own domain. The award is jointly established with Cancer Australia and funded by the Australian Government through Cancer Australia, which matches the record's awarding_body. This is the awarding organisation's own page, not an aggregator.
awarding_body.quote: Established by the Aurora Education Foundation (Aurora) and Cancer Australia the First Nations Cancer Scholarship (scholarship) supports Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander graduate students, health professionals, and early-career researchers to undertake full-time postgraduate study or research in a cancer-related field.

deadline.detail: The date in the record is correct: the Indigenous Pathways Portal lists the 2026 round as 'Open: 16/06/2026' and 'Close: 11/09/2026' with status 'Closed'. However, that cycle closed a month before today (12 October 2026) and no successor round dates are published on any Aurora page, so there is no deadline for a currently open cycle. Aurora's programme page itself carries no deadline at all.

eligibility.detail: Both distinct claims in the record are confirmed almost verbatim: open to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students only, undertaking full-time postgraduate study or research in a cancer-related field in health, research or policy, with a demonstrated impact on Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. The portal adds three requirements absent from the record: descent, community acceptance, and written confirmation of identity from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council.
eligibility.quote: To be eligible for the First Nations Cancer Scholarship, Indigenous students must be undertaking full-time postgraduate study or research in a cancer-related field in health, research or policy. Applicants must be also able to demonstrate how their study or research will impact Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities in improving cancer-related outcomes.

funding.detail: The record's 'Fully Funded' is supported: up to $120,000 AUD per year for up to three years, plus up to $5,000 AUD per year in tailored academic and wellbeing support, covering university fees/HECS, living expenses, travel, fieldwork and equipment. Minor caveat, not a material contradiction: Aurora's own wording is 'a contribution towards the cost of' study and the funds cannot cover expenses the university should meet.
funding.quote: Administered by Aurora, each scholarship is valued at up to $120, 000 AUD per year, for up to three years. Recipients will also have access to up to $5,000 AUD per year in tailored academic and wellbeing support.

degree_levels.detail: The portal's Study Level tags for this scholarship - 'Honours, Graduate Certificate, Graduate', 'Mid-Career Research', 'Postdoctoral', 'Postgraduate Coursework', 'Postgraduate Research' - cover the record's list. Caveat: the substantive eligibility text is narrower ('a postgraduate course (graduate certificate, masters or PhD) ... OR ... written confirmation from a recognised research institute'), so Honours and Postdoctoral are portal filter tags rather than stated eligible levels, and 'Postgraduate Certificate' appears to be a mislabel for 'graduate certificate' (which the record already lists separately).
degree_levels.quote: Study Level: Honours, Graduate Certificate, Graduate; Mid-Career Research; Postdoctoral; Postgraduate Coursework; Postgraduate Research

recommended_field_updates.verification_notes: Awarding body, eligibility, funding and degree levels re-confirmed on 12 Oct 2026 from Aurora's own programme page and Indigenous Pathways Portal listing; the record's official_source_url is live and unchanged. The 2026 round closed on 11 September 2026 and the portal status reads 'Closed'; no 2027 dates are published, so the record cannot be shown as an open cycle. Note a conflict between the two official bodies on the award window: Aurora states 'Up to four scholarships will be awarded yearly from 2024 to 2026', while Cancer Australia's programme page states 'Scholarships will be awarded each year from 2024 - 2027' (that page could not be fetched from this environment, so that wording comes from the search index only). Re-check the Indigenous Pathways Portal around mid-2027 for a new round.

notes_for_reviewer: Two decisions a human must make. (1) Openness: the only published cycle closed on 11 September 2026, before today, and Aurora's pages bound the award window to 2024-2026. If no 2027 round eventuates the record should be closed/expired rather than active; if Cancer Australia's 2024-2027 window is the correct one, a further round should appear and the deadline must be refreshed. (2) The 'Fully Funded' label: the award does cover fees, living costs and equipment up to $120k per year, but Aurora's own wording is 'a contribution towards the cost of' study and excludes costs the university should bear - worth confirming how the catalogue defines 'Fully Funded'.
